title: Predictive Batching & Quant Profiles: Operational Playbook for Continuous Cost Optimization
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Deliver a pragmatic, reproducible playbook that product, infra and platform engineers can use to continuously capture token-cost savings without regressing latency or quality. The playbook will combine predictive batching heuristics, model quantization profiles, and KV/prefix caching guidelines into a sequence of experiments, preflight checks, rollout steps, and monitoring checks. It should be prescriptive enough to run as a standard operating procedure for Dedicated and Hosted customers and include clear rollback criteria and example configs for runtime-1.22 and runtime-1.23. Outcome: 10-20% steady-state token cost reduction on identified workloads while maintaining >=99.8% query success and latency SLOs.

Scope: discovery and triage templates, a matrix of workload archetypes (chat short, chat long, embed-heavy, reranking), recommended batching/latency tradeoffs per archetype, quant profiles with quality validation prompts, cache TTL/eviction guidance, rollout gating, dashboards and alerts to detect regressions. Excludes changes to core kernel selection logic and major runtime refactors; those will be tracked as separate ENG epics.

Stakeholders: Product PM (owner), Serving Runtime, EconOps, Console/Observability, Solutions Eng. Success metrics will map to OKR: cost savings (token USD), latency P50/P95, failure rate, and number of customers migrated to recommended configs.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc with step-by-step runbook (discovery -> experiment -> rollout) published in Confluence
Automated validation harness with at least 3 workload archetypes and baseline vs quantized comparisons
Two representative customer pilots executed (internal or external) with documented results and rollback notes
Dashboards and alerting queries added to Console to surface cost/quality regressions
Runbook includes exact sample configs (batch size, batch window, quant profile id, cache TTL) for runtime-1.22 and runtime-1.23
updates: 2026-01-15 - Kickoff: aligned on target 10-20% cost reduction; identified initial pilot workloads (chat-short, embeddings-large). Assigned engineering spike to ENG-5507 for batching telemetry.

2026-01-28 - Discovery complete: observed that 40% of requests are short chats with low token output; these are high-leverage for batching but sensitive to latency SLOs. Identified quality delta concerns for 4-bit quant profiles on reranking models.

2026-02-10 - Prototype: created predictive batching shim that adjusts batch window by predicted token length percentile. Internal bench: 12% token reduction on chat-short at P95 latency +15ms. Added experimental quant profile q4v2 to test matrix.

2026-02-22 - Cross-team review: Runtime engineers requested additional safety checks (per-customer fallback) before rollout. Observability team proposed two new Console widgets for per-route token economics. Scheduling a follow-up to finalize alert thresholds.

2026-03-03 - Pilot planning: selected two internal customers and one external early-adopter for pilots; drafted pilot runbook and consent language. Created feature flag flow for canary and automatic rollback based on quality regressions >1.5% or latency p95 increase >10%.

2026-03-10 - Blocker noted: quantized model inference shows sporadic tokenization edge cases for certain prompt templates. Decision: hold q4 rollout for rerank flows until patch from Model Onboarding team. Proceed with batching + cache pilots for chat/embedding workloads.
risks: Quality regression risk for aggressive quantization on reranking and code-generation style prompts
Latency SLO violations if batching window mis-tuned for bursty traffic patterns
Operational complexity: additional per-route config increases support burden
Customer trust: unexpected output changes may cause churn if communication is insufficient

Implement Console cost-impact widgets and per-route rollback toggle
